newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Wife says Ethiopian dictator threatened journalist.
newsitem.headline: Wife says Ethiopian dictator threatened journalist.

text.p: The wife of Ethiopia's leading journalist missing since 1984 said on Tuesday he told her dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam threatened him before he disappeared.

"Baalu told me dictator Mengistu summoned him to his office and vented his anger and threatened him over the book he had published exposing the horror of the Marxist Revolution," the 55-year-old wife of Baalu Girma told an Addis Ababa court.

"When Mengistu asked him how can he debase the revolution in such a manner, Baalu shot back saying he had written what he believed in, to expose the weak side of the revolution so it could be corrected."
The book "Oromaie" was a satire about the Dergue Marxist military junta headed by Mengistu. The Dergue ordered it taken from shops and branded anyone with it a counter-revolutionary.

Baalu was a deputy information minister when he wrote the book but was dismissed and disappeared in 1984. A driver told the court last week he last saw him in severe pain after being tortured in 1984.

Baalu's wife was testifying at the trial of 71 former Dergue officials accused of genocide and crimes against humanity are on trial in the capital. They face the death penalty if they are found guilty.
Under court rules, Baalu's wife as a witness cannot be identified by name.
Only 46 of the 71 accused are in court in Addis Ababa. The others, including Mengistu who ruled Ethiopia from 1977 to 1991 and now lives in Zaimbabwe, are being tried in absentia.
On Monday Olympic marathon gold medallist Mamo Wolde and 127 others went on trial charged with crimes during the 1970s Red Terror campaign under the Dergue.
The 128 were allegedly involved in crimes in Addis Ababa during the Red Terror campaign, in which tens of thousands of opponents of the military regime were killed and tortured.
